blocks.note: NOT CERTIFIED. Root cause, corrected: the earlier note blamed a missing OCR fixture. The fixture is not the blocker. For ANY input that resolves to an existing file, process() -> _process_image() -> _detect_markup(), whose first statement is an unconditional `from app.core.redline import detect_redlines, summarize_markup` OUTSIDE the function's try. app/core/redline.py does not exist in this repository, and neither does app/core/image_quality.py (imported for summarize_ocr_quality at ocr.py:199 and deskew at ocr.py:348). So every image and every PDF raises ModuleNotFoundError before a pixel is read, and UniversalBlock.execute swallows it into a generic error envelope -- which is why the block looked certifiable. app/blocks/ocr_v2.py:192 has the same dead import. tests/blocks/test_ocr_real_payload.py asserts the four error payloads process() can still produce and pins the ModuleNotFoundError so the gap is executable rather than a note; those two pins must be replaced with assertions on extracted text when app.core.redline and app.core.image_quality land. Fixing this needs block/platform source, which is out of scope for a coverage lane.

blocks.note: Certified 2026-09-20 on the entry point; the 374-line geometry suite verified 2026-09-21. The earlier CAVEAT is cleared: tests/blocks/test_clash_resolver.py is behind a module-level pytest.importorskip('trimesh') and had skipped everywhere, so pytest exited 5 on that path alone. trimesh==4.12.2 made it RUN and it went RED in CI (BAR3 baseline, run 35504322136): 3 of 33 failed because bare trimesh has no boolean or ray backend -- _would_create_new_clash returned None for every candidate, so a move into a wall was proposed and a boxed-in element never escalated. Root cause was two undeclared optional backends, manifold3d and rtree (trimesh's own `easy` extra names both; block_store/kits/mep_coordination/manifest.json already declared manifold3d, rtree was declared nowhere). With both pinned, 46/46 pass across test_clash_resolver.py + test_clash_resolver_entrypoint.py + test_geometry_engine.py. No block source was changed. The entry-point file deliberately needs no geometry backend -- its elements carry mesh=None so _would_create_new_clash returns before importing geometry_engine -- and covers the gravity fall constraint, the candidate-set ordering, the flagged-vs-proposed distinction and both advertised refusals.
